README 節錄： HatchZip Extract huge archives in place. The archive shrinks as your files hatch, so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive. hatchzip.dev | Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing HatchZip is a free, open-source archive extractor for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a desktop app and a command line tool. It extracts ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar and split archives in place, for when there is not enough disk space to extract an archive next to itself, such as a large game download on a nearly full disk. Download it from hatchzip.dev. A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. title: Snapintosh/Snapintosh
body:
EL2 hypervisor and toolchain that boots macOS on the ASUS A16 (Snapdragon X2 Elite), with an Adreno Metal/IOGPU stack

README 節錄：# Snapintosh Snapintosh boots Apple's macOS 27 (build 26A428) on an ASUS Zenbook A16 laptop with a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite (X2E-96-100). It is an EL2 monitor (hypervisor) and the toolchain around it. The monitor runs Apple's stock kernelcache (the J700/T8140 kernel) unmodified by default. It supplies the platform contracts that the kernel expects from Apple silicon: the SPTM and TXM monitor calls, translation of the kernel's 16 KiB page tables, and the Apple devices the kernel looks for. Graphics run on the laptop's own Adreno X2-90 GPU through a driver stack written for this project: - **AdrenoMetal.bundle**: a Metal driver plug-in. - **AdrenoX2**: an IOGPU kernel extension, with **AdrenoDisplay** driving the internal panel. - **air2ir3**: a shader compiler that translates Apple's AIR (Metal's IR) into Mesa's ir3 for the Adreno. There is no software, CPU or paravirtual rendering path. The project also includes an I2C-HID keyboard and touchpad driver (SnapI2CHID), native QCC2072 Wi-Fi work, and NVMe storage through an emulated Apple storage controller. Snapintosh is used together with q1n1, a UEFI EL2 proxy forked from Asahi Linux's m1n1. q1n1 takes the machine at EL2 after UEFI and serves m1n1's proxy protocol over USB-C to a Mac host, which drives Snapintosh from there. ## Status This is experimental software, written for one laptop model. |

README 節錄： # Beautiful Rust Three standard Agent Skills and a lints config that teach coding agents to write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic Rust: - **`rust-best-practices`** loads whenever an agent writes or changes Rust, and steers it toward idiomatic, robust, maintainable code. - **`rust-review`** reviews existing Rust code, a file, a crate, or a diff, and writes a prioritized report where every finding cites the rule it breaks and shows the fix. - **`rust-port`** ports C, C++, Python, Go, or JavaScript to idiomatic Rust with the same behavior, porting the original tests first so you can prove the two match. - **`lints/`** is a drop-in clippy configuration that enforces the machine-checkable rules in CI. Flare is a local inference server for NVIDIA SM120/SM121 GPUs, built for long conversations, coding agents, and repeated tool use. Its goal is to make the memory, bandwidth, and compute in workstations and compact systems such as DGX Spark go further, while keeping generation responsive. README 節錄：# gdirect 中文 · Changelog gdirect browses, downloads, uploads and mounts your Google Drive from the terminal. It finds Google IPs that are reachable from your network and sends Drive traffic straight to them, with multi-connection, resumable downloads. ## How it works | Traffic | Route | | --- | --- | | Drive API, downloads, uploads (`browse`, `ls`, `download`, `upload`) | A scanned Google IP. The hostname and certificate check stay the same. If connections carrying the real SNI are reset, gdirect automatically retries under a forged identity (`g.cn` as TLS name, the real host in the Host header) — same idea as Sheas-Cealer — and remembers what worked per IP | | Sign-in and token refresh (`oauth2.googleapis.com`) | Your normal system network (DNS, proxy) | | `mount` (rclone) | Your normal system network | The first transfer command scans candidate IPs automatically and keeps the fastest working one for 24 hours. `login` and `mount` do not scan. Each candidate is probed with the real SNI first, then with the forged identity, so the stored route always reflects what actually connects. Certificates are verified against Google's own GTS roots (embedded in the binary), never against a system CA bundle — a compromised third-party CA cannot impersonate Google for gdirect.
